# `ecommerce_customer_email_valid`

> Transactional email (receipts, shipping) needs a deliverable address.

| | |
|---|---|
| Domain | [ecommerce](README.md) |
| Layer | **silver** — evaluated by the `silver` gate |
| Model | `slv_ecommerce__customers` (`ecommerce_silver.slv_ecommerce__customers`) |
| Column | `email` |
| Check | `matches_pattern` |
| Severity | `error` — a violation **stops the pipeline** |
| Defined in | [dbt/models/ecommerce/silver/_silver.yml](../../../dbt/models/ecommerce/silver/_silver.yml) |

## What it checks

`email` matches the regular expression `^[^@[:space:]]+@[^@[:space:]]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$`.

## When it fails

The `silver` task of `medallion_ecommerce` fails, gold and `publish_gold` don't run, and the batch is never added to `ecommerce_gold`: consumers keep the batches published before. `quality_report` marks the run as blocked and sends the alert, if one is configured.

The rows that broke the rule in its latest evaluation are kept in `dq_audit.ecommerce_customer_email_valid`.

## Tested by

Scenario **`invalid_emails`**: customer emails that are not valid addresses.

```bash
make generate DOMAIN=ecommerce SCENARIO=invalid_emails BATCH=2026-10-20_invalid_emails
make pipeline DOMAIN=ecommerce BATCH=2026-10-20_invalid_emails
```
